intelligence.human_view: This is the difference between a chain that is claimed and a chain that is proven. The nine Smart Links were already there — minted on November 6th, sitting in the system, waiting — so nothing had to be invented, only connected. Each one was curled and each one answered 302 to exactly the right PayPal plan, no exceptions. And then the proof that matters most: one real click on power-monthly moved the count from 110 to 111, and the dimension rows added up to 111 — direct and external, desktop, US and Canada — the who, what, where, how and when, all present and all adding up. A click is no longer invisible. It lands in the system before PayPal opens. The buttons carry no PayPal links anymore at all — grep zero — so every join now passes through the instrumentation first.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a shop with a little bell on the door. Every time someone comes in, the bell rings, and the shop writes it down — who came, what they picked, when they came. The bell is the smiley on the door: you tap the smiley, and the shop remembers. And the shop's name has no dash in it, dear — one clean word, easy to remember.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it is like a guest book at the front door, dear. Every visitor signs it, dear — who, what, when — and the book remembers, dear. And the house rules are written in plain words, dear, with no dashes to trip over, dear — thankyou, one clean word, dear.
intelligence.naya_view: I wire the tracking automatically — never fake it, never invent a link. The nine Smart Links already existed (minted 2026-11-06, owner flagship-personal); I verify each 302s to its exact PayPal plan, I prove one real click lands in smart_link_daily_stats (110 → 111, dimensions summing to 111), and I re-point the nine buttons so no PayPal URL remains in the page. A flag from one seat is a claim from inside one brief — I check it against the record before I repeat it. The thank-you return link, Auto Return, and webhooks stay open and named, never silently assumed.
